title: Sigma
caption: Jason Sanjay shows visual confidence. The writing hasn't caught up yet.
audienceSplit: The more positive response came from viewers who enjoyed Sundeep Kishan, the commercial scale, action, comedy and Jason Sanjay's confidence as a debut filmmaker. The resistance came from viewers who wanted a smarter heist, stronger tension, deeper characters and a screenplay less dependent on familiar commercial ingredients.
firstHalf: The film establishes its money, crime and heist machinery with energy, but spends too much time assembling ingredients instead of creating urgency. The emotional reason for Guru entering this world needed to become more important than the mechanics surrounding him.
interval: The interval is one of the places where Sigma finally finds the pulse a heist film needs. It creates momentum and briefly makes the film feel sharper than the setup preceding it.
secondHalf: The second half needed to convert that momentum into strategy, danger and surprise. Instead, familiarity begins winning over tension. The film keeps moving, but movement and suspense are not the same thing.
hero: Sundeep Kishan gives Guru ease, humour and enough personality to keep him watchable. The screenplay needed to make his desperation and emotional stakes as memorable as his commercial moments.
heroine: Faria Abdullah brings presence, but the female character needed stronger influence over the central narrative rather than remaining secondary to the heist machinery.
villain: A heist becomes exciting when failure feels dangerous. The opposing forces needed more intelligence and unpredictability so Guru's plan felt genuinely threatened.
director: Jason Sanjay's debut shows visual confidence and willingness to mount a commercial film. His next improvement must be screenplay control: deciding what to remove, when to accelerate and why every scene deserves to exist.
writing: This is Sigma's central weakness. Gangsters, casino, money, vaults, comedy, romance, action and twists create quantity, but not automatically tension. The screenplay needed fewer ingredients and stronger cause-and-effect between them.
music: Thaman gives the film commercial energy and helps several sequences move. But music can increase momentum only when the scene underneath already contains dramatic pressure.
songs: The songs contribute to the commercial package, but a heist narrative benefits when every interruption either develops character or increases anticipation.
editing: The film needed a more ruthless rhythm. A heist should feel as if the clock is always moving even when no literal countdown exists.
cinematography: Visual confidence is one of Jason's clearest strengths. The film understands scale, movement and commercial framing better than its debut status might suggest.
producer: The production gives a debut filmmaker meaningful scale. The lesson is that screenplay development should receive the same confidence and investment as mounting the finished film.
worked: Sundeep Kishan, visual ambition, production scale, portions of the action and comedy, and a debut director willing to attempt a full commercial canvas.
failed: Familiar heist writing, insufficient suspense, underdeveloped emotional stakes, uneven pacing and too many commercial ingredients competing for screenplay space.
heroLesson: Choose roles where the audience cares about what the character may lose, not only whether the hero can carry the commercial moments.
directorLesson: Your visual instinct is already visible. Now become ruthless about screenplay structure and scene purpose.
writerLesson: A heist is not exciting because the plan is complicated. It is exciting because the audience understands enough of the plan to fear what can destroy it.
musicLesson: Use the score to tighten existing tension, not to simulate tension the screenplay has not created.
editorLesson: Make the audience feel a clock even when the screenplay does not show one.
producerLesson: For a promising debut filmmaker, the most valuable investment before the next large set may be additional screenplay development.
oneChange: Give Guru one emotionally powerful reason to need the money, then build a cleaner heist around that desperation with fewer distractions and a genuinely intelligent opposing force.
finalDiagnosis: Sigma proves Jason Sanjay can mount a movie. His next film has to prove he can control one.
